name: William R. Berkley Jr
current_role: President & CEO (and, since June 2026, Chairman) of W. R. Berkley Corporation
profile: W. Robert Berkley Jr. is the son of William R. Berkley, who founded commercial insurer W. R. Berkley Corp. in 1967 with $2,500 while studying for his Harvard MBA. The son joined the company in 1997, became President & CEO in 2015 (per Wikipedia), and was named chairman after his father died in June 2026.
interesting_fact: W. R. Berkley was founded in 1967 with $2,500 while the elder Berkley was an MBA student at Harvard; it grew into one of the largest US commercial lines insurers.
notes: IDENTITY: the Hurun $4.2B entry most likely reflects the founder William R. Berkley (not Jr.), who DIED in June 2026 aged 80 (source above). This record describes the living son W. Robert Berkley Jr. IR contact per company releases: Karen A. Horvath, VP External Financial Communications, (203) 629-3000 (corporate line); no published email found.

name: GM Rao
current_role: Founder Chairman, GMR Group (infrastructure: airports, energy, highways, urban development)
profile: Grandhi Mallikarjuna Rao (b. 1950, Rajam, Andhra Pradesh) is a mechanical engineer who built GMR Group from a single jute mill bought in 1978 into one of India's largest infrastructure developers, running Delhi and Hyderabad airports plus energy and highway assets. He funded the move into power by selling his Vysya Bank stake; sons and family now run day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: He used the roughly Rs 3.4 billion from selling his entire ING Vysya Bank stake to fund GMR's entry into power and infrastructure; the group is also co-owner of IPL cricket team Delhi Capitals.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he worked as a shift engineer at a paper mill and then as a junior engineer in the Andhra Pradesh Public Works Department; he moved into commodities trading at his mother's insistence.
notes: Press email reported from GMR's media page (page returned 503 when re-checked; verify). Philanthropy via GMR Varalakshmi Foundation (est. 1991). Strong energy/infrastructure fit for the podcast.

name: Daniel S. Loeb
current_role: Founder and CEO, Third Point LLC (hedge fund / activist investor, New York)
profile: Dan Loeb founded Third Point in 1995 with about $3 million and built it into a major activist hedge fund managing roughly $24 billion at end-2025, known for pointed letters to boards (Yahoo, Sony, Nestle, Disney). Recent positions include SK Hynix, Siemens Energy, Vistra and Microsoft, giving him an AI/power angle.
interesting_fact: Third Point's top Q4 2025 contributors included SK Hynix and Siemens Energy, with power producer Vistra among its holdings: a direct bet on the AI data-center and energy buildout.
deep_cut_fact: At age 12 he started a skateboard company, making boards for his friends; he is a lifelong surfer who grew up near the beach in Southern California.
notes: No published press email on Third Point's site; ir@ is investor-focused. Third Point's quarterly investor letters are public and a good conversation hook.

name: William Wrigley Jr
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Wrigley Management (Chicago single-family office) and WWJr. Enterprises (venture/PE vehicle)
profile: William "Beau" Wrigley Jr., great-grandson of the gum company's founder, ran Wm. Wrigley Jr. Co. from 1999, bought Altoids and Life Savers in 2005 and sold the firm to Mars for $23 billion in 2008. He later led cannabis firm Surterra/Parallel (2018 to ~2022) and now invests through his family office.
interesting_fact: His great-grandfather originally sold baking soda and switched to gum after noticing the gum he gave away as a premium was more popular than the product.
deep_cut_fact: He is a trustee of Conservation International, where he co-chairs its Ocean Health Council, and sits on the National Geographic Society's Council of Advisors.
notes: No published email or contact form found for Wrigley Management. Was an early chairman/investor in health-kiosk startup higi (MobiHealthNews 2016). Avoid Parallel lawsuits topic.

name: Chen Mingyong
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, OPPO (Guangdong Oppo Mobile Telecommunications)
profile: Chen Mingyong (Tony Chen, b. 1969, Wanyuan, Sichuan) studied at Zhejiang University, then followed Duan Yongping from Subor to BBK. He took over BBK's audio-visual business and the OPPO brand, launched OPPO's first phone in 2008, and built it into one of the world's top smartphone makers. He remains CEO and rarely gives interviews.
interesting_fact: He was one of six people who left Subor (Xiaobawang) with Duan Yongping in 1995 to start BBK, the group from which OPPO, vivo and OnePlus all descend.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Zhejiang University's information and electronic engineering department in 1992, he worked 1992-1995 at Zhongshan Subor (Xiaobawang) Electronics, the 'learning machine'/game-console maker, rising to assistant general manager.
notes: Very media-shy. press@oppo.com is the media contact in OPPO's Oct 2025 Find X9 global release (wire copy; could not re-load to verify). The SEC-insider tag 'UMC Vice President' in the input is likely a different person with the same romanized name; disregard.

name: Segolene Gallienne
current_role: Head of Champagne Lenoble (Damery) since 2023; director of Christian Dior SE, Groupe Bruxelles Lambert, Power Corporation of Canada and Château Cheval Blanc
profile: Ségolène Frère-Gallienne is the daughter of the late Albert Frère, Belgium's richest industrialist, and co-heir to the Frère holding with stakes in GBL (run by her husband Ian Gallienne). After PR roles at Belgacom/Proximus and five years leading communications at Dior Fine Jewelry, she sits on several boards and since 2023 runs the family's Lenoble Champagne house.
interesting_fact: She sits on the board of Château Cheval Blanc, the Saint-Émilion first growth co-owned by the Frère family and Bernard Arnault, and has been a director of Christian Dior SE since about 2010.
deep_cut_fact: She has a long-standing passion for gemology, and at Lenoble she has personally joined the grape harvest to understand the terroir; she redesigned the house's HQ with Dior Maison creative director Cordelia de Castellane as a free-to-visit family home.
notes: Contacts are for Champagne Lenoble (the business she runs), not personal. Private family; GBL press office is an alternative route. Weak fit for energy/data-center themes beyond GBL holdings.

name: Camilla de Godoy Bueno Grossi
current_role: Shareholder/heir in Diagnósticos da América SA (Dasa); no public executive role found
profile: Camilla de Godoy Bueno Grossi is the daughter of Edson de Godoy Bueno (d. 2017), who co-founded Brazilian health insurer Amil and sold most of it to UnitedHealth for $4.9 billion in 2012. She and her brother Pedro Bueno (Dasa's president) inherited large stakes in lab-diagnostics group Dasa. She keeps a very low public profile; listed as UK-resident.
interesting_fact: Her father Edson Bueno, Brazil's richest healthcare billionaire, sold Amil to UnitedHealth for $4.9 billion in 2012, the source of the family's fortune.
notes: Very private; no personal public presence found. Only route is via Dasa IR (company contact, not hers). Low fit for the podcast.

name: Anand Suresh Deshpande
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Persistent Systems (Pune); stepped back from CEO role in 2019
profile: Anand Deshpande (IIT Kharagpur B.Tech; Indiana University PhD, 1989) founded Persistent Systems in Pune in 1990 with about Rs 2 lakh of own and borrowed money and built it into a listed global software/AI engineering firm (Q2 FY27 revenue $487.6M; 2026 takeover offer for Nagarro). Through the family's deAsra Foundation he supports small 'nano-entrepreneurs'.
interesting_fact: deAsra Foundation, named from his family's initials, has supported more than 750,000 nano-entrepreneurs with free help on registrations, finance and business setup.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Persistent he worked as a Member of Technical Staff at Hewlett-Packard Laboratories in Palo Alto (1989-1990), after a database-systems PhD at Indiana University, which later gave him its School of Informatics Career Achievement Award.
notes: Accessible, entrepreneurship-focused founder who speaks often at Indian tech/startup events; strong fit for an entrepreneurship podcast. deAsra (deasra.in) is another route.

name: Sathien Sathientham
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman/Vice Chairman, Carabao Group PCL (Thailand) (title varies by source)
profile: Sathien Sathientham (formerly Sathien Setthasit) co-founded Carabao in 2002 with folk-rock star Aed Carabao (Yuenyong Opakul); Carabao Dang outsells Red Bull in Thailand and the group listed in 2014. He has since pushed into large-scale beer brewing, packaging and cans; his sons run Carabao and CJ Express.
interesting_fact: Carabao is title sponsor of the English Football League Cup (the 'Carabao Cup'), and its energy drink outsells Red Bull in Red Bull's birthplace, Thailand.
deep_cut_fact: Before energy drinks he started out in real estate, and in 1999 he had early success pairing house-brewed beer with Thai food at Tawandang German Brewery in Bangkok, where he has been a director since 1999.
notes: One sponsored Khaosod piece credits Supote Teerawatanachai as Tawandang's founder, so say 'Tawandang' carefully (he is at least a long-time director). Searches may need both surnames (Setthasit/Sathientham).

name: Chen Guihua
current_role: Co-listed (with Wang Shuifu) as owner of Xizi United Holdings (Hangzhou); no public executive role found
profile: Hurun lists Chen Guihua jointly with Wang Shuifu, who founded Hangzhou Xizi Elevator Factory in 1981 and built it into Zhejiang Xizi United Holdings, spanning elevators (former Xizi Otis JV from 1997), boilers, parking systems and, since 2012, aerospace components. Her exact relationship and role could not be confirmed from public sources.
interesting_fact: Wang Shuifu founded Xizi's elevator factory in 1981 in Jianqiao, Hangzhou, when elevators were still a novelty in China, and formed a joint venture with Otis in 1997.
notes: Very little public information on Chen Guihua herself (likely Wang Shuifu's spouse per Hurun's pairing, unconfirmed). Any approach would go via Xizi United Holdings / Wang Shuifu. No published contact found.

name: Luana Lopes Lara
current_role: Co-founder & COO, Kalshi (CFTC-regulated prediction-market exchange, New York)
profile: Brazilian-born Luana Lopes Lara co-founded Kalshi in 2018 with MIT classmate Tarek Mansour after quant stints including Citadel Securities. Kalshi won CFTC approval in 2020 and in 2024 launched the first legal US election contracts in a century; valuation rose to about $11B (Dec 2025) and reportedly ~$22B (May 2026), making her the youngest self-made woman billionaire.
interesting_fact: Before MIT she danced professionally for a season of 'Swan Lake' at the Salzburger Landestheater in Austria, after training at the Bolshoi Theater School in Joinville, Brazil.
deep_cut_fact: At Escola Técnica Tupy in Joinville she competed in physics and astronomy olympiads; she was admitted to Harvard, Yale and Stanford as well as MIT, and attended MIT on a Fundação Estudar scholarship. Her father is an electrical engineer who worked at IBM and her mother a math teacher.
notes: Very podcast-friendly: has appeared on Barry Ritholtz's Masters in Business (2022) and Coin Stories. Best route: X DM or Kalshi comms. No published Kalshi press email found on-site.

name: Thomas Kwok
current_role: Senior Director, Sun Hung Kai Real Estate Agency (subsidiary of Sun Hung Kai Properties), since 2020
profile: Thomas Kwok Ping-kwong is the second son of SHKP co-founder Kwok Tak-seng and, with brothers Raymond and Walter, inherited one of Hong Kong's largest developers in 1990. He was SHKP joint chairman until 2014; since 2020 he has been a senior director of the group's real estate agency arm, while his son Adam serves as an SHKP executive director.
interesting_fact: He and brother Raymond, both devout Christians, built the Noah's Ark theme park on Ma Wan island, Hong Kong, reflecting their evangelical faith.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a civil engineer (BSc, Imperial College London; MBA, London Business School), and in the 1990s set up a church in the 75th-floor pyramid atrium atop SHKP's Central Plaza tower.
notes: Sensitive history (2014 bribery conviction, released 2019); avoid in outreach. Approach via SHKP corporate communications. SHKP also runs data-centre business (SUNeVision/iAdvantage), a possible podcast angle.

name: Lord Paul
profile: Lord Swraj Paul, Baron Paul of Marylebone, founder of steel and engineering group Caparo, died in London on 21 August 2025, aged 94.
notes: DECEASED 21 Aug 2025; source: https://www.business-standard.com/india-news/nri-industrialist-swraj-paul-passes-away-in-london-at-94-125082200300_1.html . Rest skipped per instructions.

name: Leslie Alexander
current_role: Private investor; former owner of the NBA's Houston Rockets (1993-2017)
profile: Leslie Alexander (b. 1943) dropped out of Brooklyn Law School to trade bonds on Wall Street, founded The Alexander Group in 1980 and profited from a stake in student-loan securitizer First Marblehead. He bought the Houston Rockets for $85M in 1993, won titles in 1994 and 1995, and sold the team to Tilman Fertitta for $2.2B in 2017. He now invests privately and funds animal-welfare causes.
interesting_fact: He paid $85 million for the Rockets in 1993 and sold for $2.2 billion in 2017; Forbes named him the NBA's best owner in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: He also owned the WNBA's Houston Comets (1997-2007), which won the league's first four championships (1997-2000); and he tried to buy the NHL's Edmonton Oilers in 1998.
notes: Very private since selling the Rockets; no published office/foundation contact found. Philanthropy via Clutch City Foundation (Rockets era) and a horse sanctuary in Middleburg, VA named after his mother Evelyn. Weak fit for energy/data-center themes.

name: Valery Kogan
current_role: Former chairman of the supervisory board, Moscow Domodedovo Airport (no current role; airport nationalised in 2025)
profile: Valery Kogan was a co-owner and long-time supervisory-board chairman of Moscow's Domodedovo Airport alongside main owner Dmitry Kamenshchik. In 2025 a Russian court transferred the airport's holding company to the state, and in early 2026 it was sold to a Sheremetyevo subsidiary; he no longer appears on billionaire lists.
notes: Not a viable outreach target: subject of 2025 nationalisation proceedings, asset freezes and a Russian travel ban (zona.media 27 Oct 2025, https://zona.media/news/2025/10/27/airport). No public contact. Recommend skipping.

name: Katharina Otto-Bernstein
current_role: Filmmaker and writer; co-founder/president of Film Manufacturers Inc. (New York); shareholder in Otto Group, ECE and Paramount Group
profile: Daughter of Otto Group founder Werner Otto, Katharina Otto-Bernstein inherited minority stakes in the Hamburg retail empire (incl. Crate & Barrel), shopping-centre developer ECE and US office landlord Paramount Group. A Columbia MFA, she writes, directs and produces documentaries such as Beautopia (1998), Absolute Wilson (2006) and Mapplethorpe: Look at the Pictures (2016, HBO).
interesting_fact: Her Mapplethorpe documentary premiered at Sundance and the Berlinale, aired on HBO and earned two Emmy nominations; she also sits on the Metropolitan Opera board.
deep_cut_fact: As an undergraduate she worked for Town & Country and wrote a lifestyle column for German Vogue; her first documentary, Beautopia, premiered at Sundance, was nominated for its Grand Jury Prize and won a Silver Hugo in Chicago. She chairs the Dean's Council of Columbia's School of the Arts.
notes: Contacts are for her production company Film Manufacturers Inc. A fellow media-maker angle (filmmaking/storytelling) may resonate more than business themes.

name: Zhao Bin
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Agora, Inc. (NASDAQ: API; Agora and Shengwang brands)
profile: Bin 'Tony' Zhao (Peking University, radio & electronics, 1992) was a founding engineer at WebEx, founded NeoTasks, then served as CTO of live-streaming platform YY before founding Agora in 2013-14. Agora provides real-time voice/video and, increasingly, conversational-AI APIs to developers (Q2 2026 revenue $40.4M, +18% YoY), with its Shengwang division serving China.
interesting_fact: Before Agora he was CTO of YY Inc. (2008-2013), the Chinese live-streaming pioneer, where real-time voice/video at massive scale inspired Agora's API business.
deep_cut_fact: As a founding engineer at WebEx (1997-2004) he developed the audio and video technology for what the company calls the industry's first web-collaboration product, years before Cisco bought WebEx for $3.2B.
notes: Founder is technical and has spoken at SXSW (PR Newswire 2018); conversational-AI voice infrastructure is a good AI/data-center angle.
